heading: Karnataka bandh highlights: ‘Happy news’, says CM DK Shivakumar as Kannada activists withdraw shutdown call
paragraphs:
Karnataka bandh highlights: Kannada groups on Thursday called off their Karnataka bandh after holding talks with chief minister DK Shivakumar. Shivakumar confirmed the decision and said, "All the Kannada activists met me. They have withdrawn their bandh call." "Today is the first day of the Assembly after I took over as the chief minister. I thank all the activists," he said, as per news agency ANI.

Activist arrested

Kannada activist Vatal Nagaraj was taken into preventive custody from his residence in Bengaluru on Thursday before he could join the planned protests. Police took Nagaraj into custody from his residence in Dollars Colony in the city after he refused to come out.

He had reportedly planned a rally from the BMTC-KSRTC bus stand to Town Hall and then to Freedom Park, where a protest was to be held.

Bandh call receives mixed response

Normal life mostly remained unaffected in Karnataka on Thursday, August 13, during the day-long shutdown call given by various Kanada and farmer organisations over the Cauvery water-sharing dispute with Tamil Nadu. Schools, banks, hospitals, pharmacies, public transport and other essential services will operate normally in Karnataka today as many of the organisations have extended moral support to the bandh call.

The Karnataka bandh will remain in effect from 6 am to 6 pm on Thursday, August 13.

Bengaluru Police appeal for peace

Meanwhile, the Bengaluru City Police have appealed for calm and cooperation ahead of the 'Karnataka Bandh' called for August 13, 2026, in protest against the Cauvery Water Management Authority's order on Cauvery water allocation to Tamil Nadu.

In a press note issued, the Commissioner of Police said several organisations have called for the bandh, while other organisations have informed police that they are not supporting it.

The Bengaluru City Police stated that they fully respect citizens' democratic right to protest peacefully within the law. At the same time, police said it is equally important to respect the right of other citizens to carry out daily activities without obstruction.

"All organisations and members of the public are requested to cooperate with the Bengaluru City Police in maintaining peace, public order and normalcy in the city," the note said.

What is open, what is closed amid shutdown call?

Schools, banks and hospitals will function per normal.

Public transport will also remain unaffected as Bangalore Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) and Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) employees' association have not provided support to the bandh. So are the private bus associations, transporters and autorickshaw associations, who have distanced themselves from the bandh.

Similarly, street vendors will also function as usual because everyone is only extending moral support.

Sporadic protests by farmers and Kannada organisations in Karnataka broke out against the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) order directing the state to release 12,000 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days from August 12.

Farmer organisations staged demonstration in Mandya, while various Kannada organisations gave a call for a Karnataka Bandh on August 13 in protest against the order.

The CWMA has directed Karnataka to comply with the decision of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) to release 12,000 cusecs daily for 15 days, with the water to be realised at Biligundlu.

Why farmers, Kanada organisations are protesting

Sporadic protests by farmers and Kannada organisations in Karnataka broke out against the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) order directing the state to release 12,000 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days from August 12.
Farmer organisations staged demonstration in Mandya, while various Kannada organisations gave a call for a Karnataka Bandh on August 13 in protest against the order.
The CWMA has directed Karnataka to comply with the decision of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) to release 12,000 cusecs daily for 15 days, with the water to be realised at Biligundlu.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: The Cauvery basin does not produce the same amount of water every year. When rainfall is good, Karnataka can release water downstream without facing the same level of pressure. But when inflows are poor, Karnataka wants to conserve water while Tamil Nadu still needs water for its downstream requirements.
That is why the dispute repeatedly returns during periods of deficient rainfall.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: Mekedatu has become a major part of Karnataka's political response to the Cauvery dispute. Karnataka wants to build a reservoir project there, arguing that it would help regulate water and meet Bengaluru's drinking-water requirements.
Tamil Nadu has opposed the project, fearing that a reservoir controlled by Karnataka could affect downstream flows.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: Tamil Nadu says Karnataka must release the water it is entitled to under the Cauvery-sharing framework. Karnataka says the current release demand is too high given its water situation and that it must first protect drinking water and agriculture. The legal system and Cauvery management bodies are caught between those competing claims.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: The bandh did not have unanimous support even among Kannada organisations. Several groups later said they supported the Cauvery cause but not a complete shutdown, weakening the protest's impact in Bengaluru and other urban centres.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: Farmers in the Cauvery basin depend on the river and reservoirs for cultivation. Protesters in Mandya have argued that releasing water to Tamil Nadu could leave Karnataka farmers short of water for their crops.
During the bandh, protesters even carried horse gram as a symbol of the alternative crop farmers may have to grow instead of paddy if water becomes scarce.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: The CWMA is not simply another political body. It was created following the Supreme Court's 2018 judgment to implement the Cauvery water-sharing framework. The CWRC assists it by assessing water availability and making recommendations/directions concerning releases.
So when the CWMA upholds a release direction, Karnataka faces pressure to comply even when political groups in the state strongly oppose it.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: The Cauvery conflict goes back well before the formation of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu in their present forms. The major legal framework came from the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal, followed by the Supreme Court's 2018 judgment.

In its 2018 verdict, the Supreme Court allocated 404.25 TMC to Tamil Nadu and 284.75 TMC to Karnataka, with 30 TMC for Kerala and 7 TMC for Puducherry. The judgment also led to the creation of the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) and the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) to implement and monitor the arrangement.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: The state has argued that its reservoirs have received lower-than-average inflows, making it difficult to release large quantities of water while meeting drinking-water and agricultural requirements. This is central to Karnataka's argument against the latest direction.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: The immediate trigger was the CWRC direction that Karnataka release 12,000 cusecs daily for 15 days, beginning August 12. This followed an earlier July 28 direction for 3,500 cusecs for 15 days. Tamil Nadu had complained that Karnataka was not releasing the stipulated quantity.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: The protest was unusual because Kannada organisations were divided over whether a shutdown was necessary. While Vatal Nagaraj insisted on proceeding, other groups argued that the Cauvery issue should be supported but a complete bandh was not the answer.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: Karnataka Police issued a warning that protesters cannot force shops or institutions to close, block roads, threaten people or disrupt essential services. Police said violence, property damage and traffic obstruction would invite legal action.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: The Mysuru Bar Association announced that advocates would not attend court proceedings on Thursday in protest against the CWRC direction to release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: The Mandya administration imposed a one-day ban on the sale, transportation and storage of liquor in several taluks as a precaution during the protests. Liquor shops, bars and restaurants serving alcohol were ordered to remain closed.
Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: The state government is considering legal options against the 12,000-cusec direction, including potentially approaching the Supreme Court.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: Several factions of the Karnataka Rakshana Vedike (KRV) withdrew from the bandh, citing improved reservoir inflows and assurances from the state government that it would consider approaching the Supreme Court over the 12,000-cusec order. This split significantly weakened the bandh call.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: Mandya, the epicentre of the Cauvery agitation, witnessed intense protests during the bandh. Farmers and pro-Kannada groups carried empty pots and horse gram, raised slogans including "our water, our right", and blocked the Bengaluru-Mysuru old highway. Protesters demanded that Karnataka release no further Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu, citing the state's drinking-water and agricultural needs.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: Pro-Kannada activist Vatal Nagaraj was taken into preventive custody from his Bengaluru residence on Thursday before he could join the planned bandh protests. Police detained him from Dollars Colony after he refused to come out. Nagaraj had planned a rally from the BMTC-KSRTC bus stand to Town Hall and Freedom Park. He sat inside his house with his mouth gagged as a mark of silent protest.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: Pro-Kannada groups and farmers are demanding that Karnataka prioritise its drinking-water and farming needs before releasing more Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu. They have also sought a permanent solution to the dispute, a scientific water-sharing formula for low-rainfall years and Centre-mediated talks between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. Protesters have opposed the release of 12,000 cusecs of water, citing low reservoir inflows in Karnataka.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: Mysuru and Hassan largely remained normal during the Karnataka bandh. Buses, autos and taxis operated as usual, while shops and hotels remained open. Police detained some activists who tried to block buses in Mysuru. Ballari also reported a lukewarm response, while protests were held in parts of Koppal.
Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: The Karnataka bandh called by pro-Kannada activist Vatal Nagaraj over the release of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu saw a mixed response on Thursday.

Mandya witnessed strong protests, while Bengaluru, Mysuru and several other cities remained largely normal. The bandh was called against directions to release 12,000 cusecs of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu. Several Kannada groups later withdrew support after meeting CM D K Shivakumar.
"They have said that they are withdrawing the call, which is very happy news. I congratulate them and thank them for it," Shivakumar said.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: The 2018 Supreme Court judgment set the framework for sharing Cauvery water between the states. In broad terms, Tamil Nadu receives a larger share because of its downstream dependence and historical use, while Karnataka is entitled to a substantial share for its own requirements. Actual releases can become contentious depending on reservoir storage, rainfall and inflows.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: The Supreme Court's 2018 judgment settled the broad allocation of Cauvery water between Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry, while also modifying Karnataka and Tamil Nadu's respective shares. The Cauvery Water Management Authority was subsequently created to oversee implementation and address disputes over releases.

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: The bandh call was withdrawn after Kannada activists met CM D K Shivakumar. Shivakumar said, "All the Kannada activists met me. They have withdrawn their bandh call." He also thanked the activists, saying, "Today is the first day of the Assembly after I took over as the chief minister. I thank all the activists." (ANI)

Karnataka bandh LIVE updates: Bengaluru did not completely shut down. The bandh response in Bengaluru was limited, with major public services and transport continuing to function. The impact was expected to vary across different parts of Karnataka, particularly in areas where pro-Kannada organisations have a stronger presence.
